{{Short description|American inorganic chemist}}
'''Gregory S. Girolami<ref>{{cite web|title=Link to Dr. Girolami's webpage at the Department of Chemistry at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Gregory_Girolami.html}}</ref>''' (born October 16, 1956){{Citation needed|date=June 2022}} is the William H. and Janet G. Lycan Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. His research focuses on the synthesis, properties, and reactivity of new inorganic, organometallic, and solid state species. Girolami has been elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kloeppel|first=James E.|title=Eleven professors at Illinois elected as 2007 AAAS Fellows|url=https://news.illinois.edu/view/6367/206496|access-date=2021-06-01|website=news.illinois.edu|language=en-US}}</ref> the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Greetings from the Department Head {{!}} Chemistry at Illinois|url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/greetings-department-head-1|access-date=2021-06-01|website=chemistry.illinois.edu}}</ref> and the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-23|title=2013 ACS Fellows|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/91/i30/2013-ACS-Fellows.html|access-date=2021-06-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923195815/https://cen.acs.org/articles/91/i30/2013-ACS-Fellows.html|archive-date=2020-09-23}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
He was born in 1956<ref>{{Cite web|title=Girolami, Gregory S. 1956-|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n98015422/}}</ref> in [[Honolulu, Hawaii]], and grew up in [[California]], [[Mexico]], and [[Missouri]].{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} He started college at the age of 16,{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} and four years later received B.S. degrees both in chemistry and in physics from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=X-Ray Crystallography, by Gregory S. Girolami, published by University Science Books|url=https://www.uscibooks.com/girolami.htm|access-date=2021-05-31|website=www.uscibooks.com}}</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. in 1981 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] with Prof. [[Richard A. Andersen (chemist)|Richard A. Andersen]]. Girolami's doctoral research centered on the chemistry of quadruply-bonded dinuclear transition metal complexes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Mainz|first2=Vera V.|last3=Andersen|first3=Richard A.|date=1980-04-01|title=Coordination complexes of tetrakis(trifluoroacetato)dimolybdenum. A solution proton, fluorine-19, and phosphorus-31 nuclear magnetic resonance and infrared spectroscopic study|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ic50206a004|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=19|issue=4|pages=805–810|doi=10.1021/ic50206a004|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Andersen|first2=Richard A.|date=1981-07-01|title=Reaction of binuclear carboxylate complexes of molybdenum, rhenium, ruthenium, and rhodium with tert-butyl isocyanide: metal-metal bond cleavage vs. bond retention|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ic50221a022|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=20|issue=7|pages=2040–2044|doi=10.1021/ic50221a022|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Mainz|first2=Vera V.|last3=Andersen|first3=Richard A.|last4=Vollmer|first4=Sara H.|last5=Day|first5=Victor W.|date=1981-07-01|title=Quadruply bonded tetramethyltetrakis(trialkylphosphine)dimolybdenum compounds: phosphine exchange kinetics, acetone formation with carbon monoxide and crystal structure of Mo2Me4(PMe3)4|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00403a069|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=103|issue=13|pages=3953–3955|doi=10.1021/ja00403a069|bibcode=1981JAChS.103.3953G |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Thereafter, he was a NATO postdoctoral fellow with Sir [[Geoffrey Wilkinson]] at the [[Imperial College London|Imperial College of Science and Technology]], and his work there focused on the synthesis and chemistry of [[first-row transition metal]]-alkyl complexes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Salt|first2=Julian E.|last3=Wilkinson|first3=Geoffrey|last4=Thornton-Pett|first4=Mark|last5=Hursthouse|first5=Michael B.|date=1983-09-01|title=Alkyl, hydride, and dinitrogen 1,2-bis(dimethylphosphino)ethane complexes of chromium. Crystal structures of Me2Cr(dmpe)2, CrH4(dmpe)2, and Cr(N2)2(dmpe)2|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00356a060|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=105|issue=18|pages=5954–5956|doi=10.1021/ja00356a060|bibcode=1983JAChS.105.5954G |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Wilkinson|first2=Geoffrey|last3=Thornton-Pett|first3=Mark|last4=Hursthouse|first4=Michael B.|date=1983-10-01|title=Hydrido, alkyl, and ethylene 1,2-bis(dimethylphosphino)ethane complexes of manganese and the crystal structures of MnBr2(dmpe)2, [Mn(AlH4)(dmpe)2]2 and MnMe2(dmpe)2|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00360a054|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=105|issue=22|pages=6752–6753|doi=10.1021/ja00360a054|bibcode=1983JAChS.105.6752G |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Wilkinson|first2=Geoffrey|last3=Galas|first3=Anita M. R.|last4=Thornton-Pett|first4=Mark|last5=Hursthouse|first5=Michael B.|date=1985-01-01|title=Synthesis and properties of the divalent 1,2-bis(dimethylphosphino)ethane (dmpe) complexes MCl2(dmpe)2 and MMe2(dmpe)2(M = Ti, V, Cr, Mn, or Fe). X-Ray crystal structures of MCl2(dmpe)2(M = Ti, V, or Cr), MnBr2(dmpe)2, TiMe1.3Cl0.7(dmpe)2, and CrMe2(dmpe)2|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1985/dt/dt9850001339|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Dalton Transactions|language=en|issue=7|pages=1339–1348|doi=10.1039/DT9850001339|issn=1364-5447|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Independent career ==
Girolami joined the faculty of the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1983. He has served as Head of the Chemistry Department twice, first from 2000 until 2005 and again from 2013 to 2016.

He is the author of several textbooks, including ''X-ray Crystallography''<ref name=":0" /> and ''Synthesis and Technique in Inorganic Chemistry.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Synthesis and Technique in Inorganic Chemistry, A Laboratory Manual|author1=Gregory S. Girolami|author2=Thomas B. Rauchfuss|author3=Robert J. Angelici|author3-link=Robert Angelici|url=http://www.uscibooks.com/rauch.htm|access-date=2021-05-31|website=www.uscibooks.com}}</ref> He was the co-editor of volume 36 of ''Inorganic Syntheses''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inorganic Syntheses, Volume 36 {{!}} Wiley|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Inorganic+Syntheses%2C+Volume+36-p-9781118744840|access-date=2021-05-31|website=Wiley.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

Girolami is also co-founder of a [[University spin-off|university spin-off company]], [http://www.tiptek.com/ Tiptek LLC], which manufactures ultrasharp probe tips for use in [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]] and for fault diagnosis and testing of [[integrated circuit]]s. The company has patented its field-directed sputter sharpening (FDSS) technology, which was originally developed in the laboratories of Girolami and fellow UIUC Professor [[Joseph Lyding]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schmucker|first1=S. W.|last2=Kumar|first2=N.|last3=Abelson|first3=J. R.|last4=Daly|first4=S. R.|last5=Girolami|first5=G. S.|last6=Bischof|first6=M. R.|last7=Jaeger|first7=D. L.|last8=Reidy|first8=R. F.|last9=Gorman|first9=B. P.|last10=Alexander|first10=J.|last11=Ballard|first11=J. B.|date=2012-07-03|title=Field-directed sputter sharpening for tailored probe materials and atomic-scale lithography|journal=Nature Communications|language=en|volume=3|issue=1|pages=935|doi=10.1038/ncomms1907|pmid=22760634|bibcode=2012NatCo...3..935S|issn=2041-1723|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Research==
To date, Girolami's independent research career has encompassed five major themes: mechanistic studies of [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic reactions]] such as the polymerization of alkenes and the activation of saturated alkanes, the [[chemical vapor deposition]] of thin films from designed molecular precursors, the construction and study of molecular analogs of the [[Photosynthetic reaction centre|photosynthetic reaction center]], actinide chemistry, and the synthesis of new molecule-based [[magnetic materials]]. His research approach emphasizes the synthesis of new inorganic and organometallic compounds and materials, investigations of their mechanisms of formation, and measurements and interpretations of their physical properties.

=== Organometallic chemistry ===
Girolami's early work focused on the synthesis of transition metal compounds with metal-hydrogen and metal-carbon bonds, especially those possessing unusual electronic structures.  In 1989, Girolami and Morse showed that {{chem|[Zr(CH|3|)|6|]|2-}} was of [[trigonal prismatic molecular geometry]] as indicated by [[X-ray crystallography]].<ref name=":1">{{cite journal|author1=Morse, P. M.|author2=Girolami, G. S.|year=1989|title=Are d<sup>0</sup> ML<sub>6</sub> complexes always octahedral? The X-ray structure of trigonal-prismatic [Li(tmed)]2[ZrMe6]|journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc.|volume=111|issue=11|page=4114|doi=10.1021/ja00193a061|bibcode=1989JAChS.111.4114M }}</ref> This rare molecular geometry was attributed to second-order [[Jahn-Teller distortion]]s in this d<sup>0</sup> metal complex. Girolami's group accurately predicted that other d<sup>0</sup> ML<sub>6</sub> species such as {{chem|[Nb(CH|3|)|6|]|-}}, {{chem|[Ta(CH|3|)|6|]|-}}, and [[Hexamethyltungsten|W(CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]] would also prove to have trigonal prismatic geometry.<ref name=":1" /> Girolami also discovered the first titanium alkyl/alkene complex in 1993, which models the key intermediate in [[Ziegler-Natta catalysis]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Spencer|first1=Michael D.|last2=Morse|first2=Paige M.|last3=Wilson|first3=Scott R.|last4=Girolami|first4=Gregory S.|date=1993-03-01|title=Preparation, catalytic reactivity, and x-ray crystal structure of the first Group 4 alkyl/alkene complexes. The first structural models of the key Ziegler-Natta catalytic intermediate|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00058a073|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=115|issue=5|pages=2057–2059|doi=10.1021/ja00058a073|bibcode=1993JAChS.115.2057S |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Later model studies of C-H, B-H, and Si-H activation by transition metal complexes led to his current work on approaches to the isolation of stable [[alkane]] complexes.

=== Chemical vapor deposition ===
In the mid-1980s Girolami began research on the [[chemical vapor deposition]] (CVD) of thin films, especially of phases containing transition metals. Girolami studied the chemical design of new CVD precursors. He investigated copper(I) compounds for copper CVD,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Jeffries|first2=Patrick M.|last3=Dubois|first3=Lawrence H.|date=1993|title=Mechanistic studies of copper thin-film growth from CuI and CuII .beta.-diketonates|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja00056a028|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=115|issue=3|pages=1015–1024|doi=10.1021/ja00056a028|bibcode=1993JAChS.115.1015G |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> an approach that is now a key fabrication step for integrated circuits.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gordon|first1=Peter G.|last2=Kurek|first2=Agnieszka|last3=Barry|first3=Seán T.|date=2014-12-09|title=Trends in Copper Precursor Development for CVD and ALD Applications|journal=ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology|language=en|volume=4|issue=1|pages=N3188–N3197|doi=10.1149/2.0261501jss|s2cid=97668427 |issn=2162-8769|doi-access=free}}</ref> His mechanistic studies of CVD processes involved transition metals, and these efforts have recently resulted in the development of low-temperature CVD to achieve the deposition of [[Conformal film|conformal thin films]], in work carried out in collaboration with Professor John Abelson of Illinois' Department of Materials Science and Engineering.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Abelson|first1=John R.|last2=Girolami|first2=Gregory S.|date=2020-04-09|title=New strategies for conformal, superconformal, and ultrasmooth films by low temperature chemical vapor deposition|journal=Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A|volume=38|issue=3|pages=030802|doi=10.1116/6.0000035|bibcode=2020JVSTA..38c0802A|issn=0734-2101|doi-access=free}}</ref> Most recently, he discovered a new class of highly volatile CVD precursors containing the aminodiboranate ligand.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Daly|first1=Scott R.|last2=Kim|first2=Do Young|last3=Yang|first3=Yu|last4=Abelson|first4=John R.|last5=Girolami|first5=Gregory S.|date=2010-02-24|title=Lanthanide N,N-Dimethylaminodiboranates: Highly Volatile Precursors for the Deposition of Lanthanide-Containing Thin Films|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja9098005|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=132|issue=7|pages=2106–2107|doi=10.1021/ja9098005|pmid=20108908|bibcode=2010JAChS.132.2106D |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Daly|first1=Scott R.|last2=Kim|first2=Do Young|last3=Girolami|first3=Gregory S.|date=2012-07-02|title=Lanthanide N,N-Dimethylaminodiboranates as a New Class of Highly Volatile Chemical Vapor Deposition Precursors|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ic201852j|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=51|issue=13|pages=7050–7065|doi=10.1021/ic201852j|pmid=22686567|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Molecular analogs of the photosynthetic reaction center ===
In a now-concluded project, Girolami studied the chemistry and photophysics of bis([[porphyrin]]ate) metal sandwich complexes in collaboration with Illinois Professor of Chemistry [[Kenneth S. Suslick]]. These complexes were proposed to mimic the conversion of light to chemical energy in photosynthesis. Girolami's group synthesized bis(porphyrin) complexes of thorium, uranium,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Gorlin|first2=Philip A.|last3=Milam|first3=Stanley N.|last4=Suslick|first4=Kenneth S.|last5=Wilson|first5=Scott R.|date=1994-06-01|title=Bis(porphyrin)actinide Complexes and Their Radical Cations and Dications|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00958979408024247|journal=Journal of Coordination Chemistry|volume=32|issue=1–3|pages=173–212|doi=10.1080/00958979408024247|issn=0095-8972|url-access=subscription}}</ref> zirconium,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Hein|first2=Christopher L.|last3=Suslick|first3=Kenneth S.|date=1996|title=A Zirconium Bis(porphyrinate) Sandwich Complex with an Appended Quinone|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/anie.199612231|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|volume=35|issue=11|pages=1223–1225|doi=10.1002/anie.199612231|issn=1521-3773|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and hafnium, and showed that these complexes displayed photophysical properties similar to those of the [[P700|“special pair”]], a chlorophyll dimer present in the [[photosystem I]] reaction center.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Girolami|first1=Gregory S.|last2=Gorlin|first2=Philip A.|last3=Suslick|first3=Kenneth S.|date=1994-02-01|title=Electronically asymmetric bis(porphyrin) sandwich complexes|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ic00082a002|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=33|issue=4|pages=626–627|doi=10.1021/ic00082a002|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Actinide chemistry ===
Overlapping with Girolami's interest in bis(porphryin) complexes that mimic the photosynthetic reaction center, the Girolami group has also studied actinide chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bilsel|first1=Osman|last2=Rodriguez|first2=Juan|last3=Milam|first3=Stanley N.|last4=Gorlin|first4=Philip A.|last5=Girolami|first5=Gregory S.|last6=Suslick|first6=Kenneth S.|last7=Holten|first7=Dewey|date=1992-07-01|title=Electronic states and optical properties of porphyrins in van der Waals contact: thorium(IV) sandwich complexes|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00042a037|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=114|issue=16|pages=6528–6538|doi=10.1021/ja00042a037|bibcode=1992JAChS.114.6528B |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Magnetic materials ===
In the mid-1990s, Girolami began an investigation of the synthesis of new magnetic solids via a building block approach, publishing in ''Science'' in 1995.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Entley|first1=William R.|last2=Girolami|first2=Gregory S.|date=1995-04-21|title=High-Temperature Molecular Magnets Based on Cyanovanadate Building Blocks: Spontaneous Magnetization at 230 K|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.268.5209.397|journal=Science|language=en|volume=268|issue=5209|pages=397–400|doi=10.1126/science.268.5209.397|issn=0036-8075|pmid=17746547|bibcode=1995Sci...268..397E|s2cid=10784183|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Girolami also reported metal-substituted analogs of [[Prussian blue]] that have magnetic ordering temperatures above 100&nbsp;°C.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Holmes|first1=Stephen M.|last2=Girolami|first2=Gregory S.|date=1999-06-01|title=Sol−Gel Synthesis of KVII[CrIII(CN)6]·2H2O: A Crystalline Molecule-Based Magnet with a Magnetic Ordering Temperature above 100 °C|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja990946c|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=121|issue=23|pages=5593–5594|doi=10.1021/ja990946c|bibcode=1999JAChS.121.5593H |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Girolami has received numerous awards for his research, including the [[Office of Naval Research]] Young Investigator Award, a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Foundation Fellowship]], a Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Award, and a University Scholar Award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gregory S. Girolami {{!}} Chemistry at Illinois|url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/ggirolam|access-date=2021-06-01|website=chemistry.illinois.edu|language=en}}</ref> He has been honored by UIUC with a Campus Award for Excellence in Graduate and Professional Teaching, for the introduction of a graduate class in inorganic chemistry covering [[group theory]] and [[electronic correlation]] methods.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bureau|first=News|title=Faculty, staff and teaching assistants honored with Campus Awards for Excellence in Instruction|url=https://news.illinois.edu/view/6367/638044|access-date=2021-06-01|website=news.illinois.edu|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Greg Girolami recognized for excellence in teaching {{!}} Chemistry at Illinois|url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/news/2018-04-13/greg-girolami-recognized-excellence-teaching|access-date=2021-06-01|website=chemistry.illinois.edu|language=en}}</ref>
